t: If the line x−1=0 is the directrix of the parabola y²−kx+8=0,k≠0 and the parabola intersects the circle x²+y²=4 in two real distinct points, then the value of k is

where  Y=y,X=x−8/k and A=k/4
Equation of the directrix is
X=−A⇒x−8/k=−k/4

For k=4, the parabola is y²=4(x−2) whose vertex is (2,0) and touches the circle x²+y²=4 at the vertex. Therefore k≠4.

t: The conic represented by the equation √ax+√by=1 is
s:
The given conic is √ax+√by=1
Squaring both sides, ax+by+2√abxy=1
or ax+by−1=−2√abxy
Squaring again, (ax+by−1)²=4abxy
or a²x²−2abxy+b²y²−2ax−2by+1=0 …(1)
Comparing the equation (1) with the equation Ax²+2Hxy+By²+2Gx+2Fy+C=0
∴A=a²,H=−ab,B=b²,G=−a,F=−b,C=1
Then, Δ=ABC+2FGH−AF²−BG²−CH²
=a²b²−2a²b²−a²b²−a²b²−a²b²=−4a²b²≠0
and H²=a² b²=AB
So we have Δ≠0 and H²−AB=0. Hence the given equation represent a parabola. .

Any point on the parabola is (at²,2at) where a=1. For the latus rectum x=a⇒t²=1⇒t=±1. So ends of latus rectum are (1,±2). Equations of the normals at these points is given by y=−tx +2at+at³
⇒ x+y−3=0 and x−y−3=0
which intersect at (3,0).

t: If the common tangent in the first quadrant of the circle x²+y²=16 and the ellipse x²/25+y²/4=1 meets the coordinate axes at A and B, the length of AB is

t: An equation of a common tangent to the parabola y²=4x and x²=4y is
s: Equation of a tangent to y²=4x is y=mx+1/m. If it touches the parabola x²=4y then the roots of the equation x²=4(mx+1/m) are coincident. So (4m)²+16/m=0⇒m=−1 and the equation of the tangent is x+y+1=0 !

t: The normal at the point (bt₁²,2bt₁) on a parabola meets the parabola again in the point (bt₂²,2bt₂), then

t: If the normal to the parabola y²=4x at P(1,2) meets the parabola again in Q, then coordinates of Q are
s: The given equation of the parabola is y²=4x Equation of tangent at (1,2) is [⇒ y⋅2 =2(x+1); ⇒ y =x+1] Slope of tangent =1 ∴ slope of the normal =−1 Equation of the normal passing through (1,2) is [ y−2=−1(x−1); y−2=−x+1⇒x+y=3] This equation again meet at Q of the parabola, then [ y²=4(3−y); ⇒ y²=12−4y⇒y²+4y−12=0; ⇒ (y−2)(y+6)=0; ⇒ y=2,6] If y=−6, then x=3−(−6)=9 ∴ The coordinates of point Q are (9,−6).

So, equation of common tangent is
[y =1/2x+1/2; ⇒ x−2y+1 =0.]

t: The locus of the point of intersection of two tangents to the parabola y²=4ax, which are at right angle to one another is
s:
Let the two tangents to the parabola y²=4 ax be PT and QT which are at right angle to one another at T(h,k). Then we have to find the locus of T(h,k)
We know that y=mx+a/m, where m is the
slope is the equation of tangent to the parabola y²=4ax for all m
[[img:e5293654b8b8]]
Since this tangent to the parabola will pass through T(h,k) so
k=mh+a/m; or m² h−mk+a=0
This is a quadratic equation in m so will have two roots, say m₁ and m₂, then m₁+m₂=k/h, and m₁:m₂=a/h
Given that the two tangents intersect at right
angle so m₁⋅m₂=−1 or a/h=−1 or h+a=0
The locus of T(h,k) is x+a=0, which is the
equation of directrix.

t: If tangents are drawn to the parabola y²=4ax at points whose abscissae are in the ratio m²:1, then the locus of their point of intersection is the curve (m>0).
s:
Consider two points P(at₁²,2at₁) and Q(at₂²,2at₂) on the parabola y²=4ax
Given :at₁²/at₂²=m²/1 or t₁=mt₂
Let R(h,k) be the point of intersection of tangents at P and Q
Then, h=at₁t₂ and k=a(t₁+t₂)…(1)
⇒ h=amt₂² and k=a(mt₂+t₂)
[Using (1)] ⇒ t₂²=h/am and t₂=k/(a(m+1))
Equating the two values of t₂, we k²/(a²( m+1)²)=h/am
⇒ k²=ah((m+1)²)/ m⇒k²=ah(√m+1/√m)²
∴  Required locus is y²=ax(m^(1/2)+m^(−1/2))²

t: If two tangents drawn from a point P to the parabola y²=4x are at right angles, then the locus of P is

t: Locus of the mid points of the chords of the parabola y²=8x which touch the circle x²+y²=4 is

ky−4(x+h)=k²−8h
⇒4x−ky+k²−4h=0
which touches the circle x²+y²=4

Locus of (h,k) is (y²−4x)²=4(16+y²)

t: A line PQ meets the parabola y²=4ax in R such that PQ is bisected at R. If the coordinates of P are (x₁,y₁) then the locus of Q is the parabola
s:

[[img:2887009ff594]]
Since R is mid point of PQ,

⇒ t²=(x₁+h)/2a and t=(y₁+k)/4a
Equating the two values of t, we get ((y₁+k)/4a)²=(x₁+h)/2a⇒(y₁+k)²=8a(x₁+h)
Hence, locus of Q(h,k) is (y+y₁)²=8a(x+x₁) .

t: If two tangents to the parabola y²=8x meet the tangent at its vertex in M and N such that MN=4, then the locus of the point of intersection of those two tangents is
s:
[[img:e1aab4d2593c]]
Given parabola is y²=8x.Comparing with y²=4ax, we get4a=8 ⇒a=2Let the parametric co-ordinates of P & Q be (at₁², 2at₁) & (at₂², 2at₂) respectively.So, equation of tangent at P is yt₁=x+2t₁² ...........(i)and the equation of tangent at Q is yt₂=x+2t₂² ...........(ii)Since, its given that tangent at the vertex meet at points M & N.So, to find M, we put x=0 in equation (i), we getyt₁=0+2t₁²⇒y=2t₁and to find N, we put x=0 in equation (ii), we getyt₂=0+2t₂²⇒y=2t₂So, the co-ordinates of M & N are (0, 2t₁) & (0, 2t₂) respectively.It is also given that MN=4.⇒|2t₁−2t₂|=4⇒|t₁−t₂|=2⇒(t₁−t₂)²=4 ..........(iii)We also know that the point of intersection of two tangent to a parabola whose parametric co-ordinates are (at₁², 2at₁) & (at₂², 2at₂) meet at R whose co-ordinates is (at₁t₂, a(t₁+t₂))=(2t₁t₂, 2(t₁+t₂))=(h, k).Now, (t₁+t₂)²=(t₁−t₂)²+4t₁t₂⇒(k/2)²=4+4(h/2) (using equation (iii))⇒k²/4=4+2h⇒k²=8(h+2)For locus of R, replacing h→x & k→y, we gety²=8(x+2)Hence, the required locus equation is y²=8(x+2).

t: A variable point P divides every chord (having slope 2) of the parabola y²=4x into two parts such that the length of one part is twice the other. If locus of P is also a parabola, then find the coordinates of focus of the locus of point P.
s:
Let AB be any chord joining the points A(t₁², 2t₁) and B(t₂², 2t₂) of the given parabola y²=4x and having slope 2.
⇒ 2/(t₁+t₂)=2
⇒ t₁+t₂=1
Let us assume that the coordinates of the point P are P(h, k)
Since, P divides AB 1: 2 in the ratio 1: 2 internally
Hence, the coordinates of P are given by
h=(2t₁²+t₂²)/(2+1),k=(4t₁+2t₂)/(2+1)
⇒ 3h=2t₁²+t₂², 3k=4t₁+2t₂
Using t₁+t₂=1 and 3k=4t₁+2t₂, we get
t₁=(3k−2)/2 and t₂=(4−3k)/2
**
[[img:eae89b44eeb3]]
**
On substituting the values of t₁ and t₂ in 3h=2t₁²+t₂², we get
3h=2((3k−2)/2)²+((4−3k)/2)²
⇒ 3h=2(9k²/4+1−3k)+(4+9k²/4−6k)
⇒ 3h=27k²/4−12k+6
⇒ 12h=27k²−48k+24
⇒ k²−16/9k−4/9h+8/9=0
Hence, the required locus is
y²−16/9y−4/9x+8/9=0
⇒ (y−8/9)²=4/9(x−2/9)
The focus of the above locus is
(x−2/9=1/9, y−8/9=0)≡(x=1/3, y=8/9)

t: A circle of radius 4, drawn on a chord of the parabola y²=8x as diameter, touches the axis of the parabola. Then, the slope of the chord is

y−4=m(x−h) …..(ii)
If line (ii) passes through the point P(2t₁², 4t₁) and Q(2t₂², 4t₂) on parabola Eq. (i), then
y(t₁+t₂)−2x−4t₁t₂=0 …..(iii)
Having slope
m=2/(t₁+t₂) …..(iv)
Since, (h, 4) is the mid - point of PQ. Therefore,
2×4=4(t₁+t₂)
⇒   t₁+t₂=2
Hence, slope of chord PQ is
m=2/2=1 [using Eq. (iv)]
